instruction: Audit the two codebases only at the pinned commits and use each in_scope_files array as the authoritative file list.
An in-scope contract includes its parent contracts; a library defect qualifies when an in-scope contract uses and is affected by it. Repository contracts outside scope do not qualify.
Apply the selected Sherlock guidelines in full, including hierarchy of truth, trust defaults, invalid and valid categories, proof-of-concept rules, and the rule for acknowledged prior-audit issues.

Use the ordered pinned severity definitions together with the guidelines’ denial-of-service conditions, quantitative loss thresholds, replay note, likelihood rule, proof-of-concept requirement, and private-mempool downgrade. Medium requires the complete conditions in both sources.

instruction: This supplied companion renders severity labels and reward weights; use severity-set.json and the selected guidelines, not the weights alone, to qualify severity.
Use this source-referenced view before comparing a target report and a potential duplicate; the selected Sherlock duplication rules have highest authority.
Use the overview to understand actors, core execution flows, and the changes introduced between 2.1.x and 2.3.0; it is orientation, not a review priority or risk ranking.

Apply the listed chain behavior and integration trust assumptions. Standard ERC20 and native ETH are supported; fee-on-transfer tokens are in scope subject to section 6, while rebasing, transfer-hook, over-limit, and self-harm-only malicious-token cases are excluded as stated.

There is no admin. The caller and calldata are trusted for the caller’s funds. User-chosen route components are untrusted, but self-harm within the user’s own bounds is invalid; harm to others or beyond those bounds is valid. Apply the source’s locker-based definition of user.
v4-core and Permit2 are dependencies outside code scope, but their documented behaviors apply. The cited v4-core audits and Known Effects of Hook Permissions remain prior-disclosure context.

The staged lib directories are empty. For dependency-complete builds, clone the public repositories at the pinned commits, initialize submodules, and follow the repository-specific commands and RPC requirement.
A valid issue must exist in the pinned 2.3.0 contest code. An issue fixed there is invalid even if it remains in an older deployment.
This document defines payout families, caps, and the live-code multiplier. It does not replace the pinned validity, scope, or severity rules.
All issues in every report listed in section 4 are known. Submissions matching any item in section 6 are invalid.

The source also identifies the 2024 Cantina v4 competition and the ongoing Uniswap Cantina bounty as disclosure sources. Their issue bodies were not supplied locally; use the local section 6 expansions and out-of-scope list, and follow the source links when a candidate may match an unexpanded disclosure.
The twelve-item 2024 Cantina v4 competition out-of-scope list still applies to this engagement, including prior-review issues and documented effects of hook permissions.

Use this locator to search every finding in the locally supplied audit reports by report, identifier, title or summary, then read the cited unchanged report section for the authoritative details and resolution notes.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.A are invalid. The section covers router custody, allow-revert behavior, decoding, reentrancy, deadlines, command types, and Across deposits; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.B are invalid. The section covers codeless tokens, permit front-running, payer rules, ETH, portions, WETH, and adapter balance commands; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.C are invalid. The section covers donations, exact-output behavior, fee and rounding, and CREATE2 pair addressing; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.D are invalid. The section covers partial fills, contract-balance donations, exact output, fee-on-transfer behavior, callbacks, and paths; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.E are invalid. The section covers supported actions, settlement and deltas, slippage and per-hop bounds, hooks, partial fills, fee-on-transfer behavior, and sender context; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.F are invalid. The section covers resolver trust, sentinel handling, register lifetime, sub-plans, failure handling, and secondary sentinel mapping; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.G are invalid. The section covers nested execution gating, shared deltas, caller responsibility, outside-unlock behavior, and other v4 commands; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.H are invalid. The section covers signed-route funding, signature coverage, replay, sender verification, and public execution context; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.I are invalid. The section covers locker identity, recipients, payer behavior, user-supplied router, sweeping, ETH, codeless tokens, fee-on-transfer, and callbacks; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.J are invalid. The section covers position-manager action filtering, approvals, sender mapping, ETH forwarding, external control, and v3 migration; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.K are invalid. The section covers permissionless fee pokes, controller lookup, and missing-adapter behavior; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.L are invalid. The section covers adapter verification, permission subject, swap-only boundaries, intermediate hops, shared underlyings, truncation, and other adapter behavior; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.M are invalid. The section covers supply limits, rebasing behavior, native Blast yield, and the continuing Cantina out-of-scope list; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

Submissions matching any item in section 6.N are invalid. The section covers contract size, optimizer choice, transient slots, lock internals, style, and duplication; preserve every condition and exception in the cited text.

executeNested is only for a contract that opened the surrounding PoolManager unlock; v4 deltas are shared for that unlock, so a permissionless path into this entrypoint can expose that contract’s capital and credit. This misuse is disclosed and accepted.

SwapProxy routes must use payerIsUser=false and explicit user recipients rather than MSG_SENDER; token inputs are intended, ETH-input actions should go directly to the router, and codeless token transfers silently succeed.
INCREASE_LIQUIDITY_FROM_DELTAS and MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS are explicitly deprecated as sandwich-vulnerable because the delta-based approach lacks minimum-liquidity slippage protection.
